upstream: Toward the water a dam holds back, against the way the river flows. In every section drawing in this book the upstream side is on the left.
downstream: Away from the water a dam holds back, the way the river flows. In every section drawing in this book it is on the right.
crest: The top of a dam: the level strip, often carrying a road, that runs along its whole length.
heel: Where the upstream face of a dam meets the ground.
toe: Where the downstream face of a dam meets the ground. Water that seeps through or under an embankment usually comes out at or near the toe, so that is where an inspector looks first.
freeboard: The height of the crest above the water behind the dam: the margin left for waves and floods before water spills over the top.
abutment: A valley side that the end of a dam rests against. The left and right abutments are named as you look downstream.
tailwater: The water on the downstream side of a dam, in the river or pond below it. The difference between the reservoir level and the tailwater level is the drop the water makes on its way past the dam.
slope-notation: A slope written as horizontal distance to vertical rise. 2H:1V, often shortened to 2:1, means two metres across for every metre up; the larger the first number, the flatter the slope.
